name: Backhand chop
summary: The backhand defensive stroke: long, down and forward, with an open bat.
whenToUse: Against loops to your backhand when you play as a defender, far from the table.

keyPoints.stance: Side-on: right foot forward for a right-hander's backhand chop (left foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Shoulders turn back with the bat, then forward into the stroke.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Long: from shoulder height across and down to the knee.
keyPoints.timing: As the ball drops, beside the body.
keyPoints.batArm: Bat open, elbow away from the body; brush down and forward under the ball.
keyPoints.recovery: Back to the middle, low and ready.
keyPoints.anticipation: Heavier spin kicks up more: keep the bat more upright. Lighter spin: open it more.

cues: Down and forward under the ball
Side-on, then back to the middle

learningPath.task: Watch the shoulder turn and the long stroke.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.
3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the bat start by your shoulder?
Did you recover to the middle?

learningPath.task: Chop slow topspin to your backhand.

gamePatterns.situation: Topspin rally that pushes you back.
gamePatterns.how: Switch to chopping: deep and low to their backhand, then vary the spin.

causes: Bat too open against heavy topspin
fixes: Keep the bat more upright against heavy loops

causes: Bat too closed against a light or slow loop
fixes: Open the bat more against light topspin

causes: Ball too close to the body
fixes: Step back and to the side

penholdNotes: Use the reverse side for backhand chops with penhold.
